name: waha
title: WhatsApp through WAHA
description: The WAHA container's API key, the key WAHA signs its webhook deliveries with, and — per machine — where the container answers and how it reaches this instance.
setup:
Set up the keys of a WAHA (WhatsApp HTTP API) container on this machine.
1. Ask the person which spare WhatsApp number to link — never the person's own number.
2. Generate and store both keys first, in one pipe: `{ printf 'WAHA_API_KEY=%s\n' "$(openssl rand -hex 24)"; printf 'WAHA_WEBHOOK_HMAC=%s\n' "$(openssl rand -hex 24)"; } | flow credentials set waha --stdin` — generated inside the pipe, so neither key passes through you.
3. Read the API key back only where the container needs it (the project's `.env.local`), never into a reply.
4. Run the container with the same API key: `docker run -d --name waha -p 3010:3000 -e WAHA_API_KEY=<api key> -e WHATSAPP_DEFAULT_ENGINE=NOWEB devlikeapro/waha`.
5. Store where the container answers and how it reaches this instance (they differ per machine): pipe `WAHA_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3010` and `WAHA_WEBHOOK_URL=http://host.docker.internal:<this instance's port>/api/v1/data_source/webhook/waha` into `flow credentials set waha --stdin`.
6. Confirm with `flow credentials check waha`. Linking the phone (scanning the QR) is the person's step. Never print or repeat a key.

WAHA_BASE_URL.label: WAHA URL
WAHA_BASE_URL.hint: Where the WAHA container answers, from this machine.

WAHA_WEBHOOK_URL.label: Webhook URL (as WAHA sees this instance)
WAHA_WEBHOOK_URL.hint: Verify registers it on the session with the signing key, so WAHA's deliveries reach this instance signed. A deployment has its own.
